_comment: VALIDATION FIXTURE. Little Rock is published (19 of 19 live since 2026-08-05) — the first 16 landed 2026-07-30 via the bespoke scripts/import-little-rock-merged.mjs, which stays in place as that batch's audit trail. This config exists so the GENERIC pipeline can be run against the same artifact and proved to reproduce the same classification. `expected_publish` below is the recorded known-good split, verified against production; --stage=project and --stage=publish both assert against it and fail the run on any divergence. If the generic pipeline ever disagrees, fix the pipeline — never edit this block to match the output.
_expected_publish_history: RE-AUTHORED 2026-08-05 from 16/19 to 19/19, and this is the one legitimate reason to rewrite the block above: the GATE changed by owner decision, not the pipeline's classification. ADR-16 released `pickleball-kingdom-little-rock-ar` (a `low`-precision coordinate now publishes behind an approximate-location label) and ADR-17 released `indianhead-park-sherwood-ar` + `tyndall-park-benton-ar` (`research_status='probable'` is no longer a gate condition). The prior block held exactly those three, for exactly those two reasons, so the divergence was fully accounted for before the expectation was touched — nothing was nudged to fit. `hold` is now empty: every row in this batch is live. The two `probable` rows were re-tiered `source_verified` -> `listed` first (scripts/retier-adr18-debt.mjs), because ADR-18 derives the tier from research_status and --stage=verify asserts the two agree.
msa: Little Rock–North Little Rock–Conway, AR (Faulkner, Grant, Lonoke, Perry, Pulaski, Saline counties)
_geocode_cache_comment: Added 2026-08-04. This was the ONLY config that omitted geocode_cache, which was harmless while every metro shared one cache file and became permanent when the cache split per metro — every config copied from this one would inherit the fallback. The fallback is now safe on its own (it resolves inside metro-research/), so this line is uniformity rather than protection: every config states where its cache lives instead of one of them leaving it implied. A unit test asserts that, so the property is checked rather than counted.

reconciles._backfill_note: These five fields were BACKFILLED on 2026-07-31, when evidence_url + adjudicated_on became mandatory on every reconcile entry. They are RECONSTRUCTED from this batch's own artifact, never invented: matched_distance_m (2), the adjudication date (the artifact's `updated` field and the batch tag are both 2026-07-30) and the evidence URL (the venue's tier-1 name.source_url, the City of Conway's own page) all come from little-rock-count/little-rock-candidates.json. Note what the SAME-VENUE verdict actually rested on, because the URL alone would misstate it: an independent Nominatim geocode resolving to the exact OSM element way/1498910770, corroborated by a unique-slug collision on the already-correct conway-community-center-conway-ar. That is geometric and key-level evidence, not a claim read off the Conway page; the Conway URL is the controlling-entity source for the venue's IDENTITY. This config is the generic pipeline's VALIDATION HARNESS for an already-published batch — the audit trail of what actually ran against production is scripts/import-little-rock-merged.mjs, which is deliberately untouched.
reconciles.note: Conway Community Center merges onto a dormant OSM row matched at 2 m. The tell was not the name or the slug (both were already correct) but the geocode resolving to the same osm_id plus a slug-collision hit.
